title: Garbage Truck Driver Salary: Award Rates, Annual Pay, and Tax Guide
description: Find the garbage truck driver salary under the Waste Management Award. Hourly rates, annual pay for 38-hour week, casual loading, super, and tax explained.
salarySummary: A full-time garbage truck driver at Level 3 under the Waste Management Award earns $31.07 per hour, or about $61,394 annually for a 38-hour week, with super and tax calculated on top.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a garbage truck driver under the Waste Management Award?
faqs.a: The minimum hourly rate for a full-time adult employee at Level 3 is $31.07 per hour (including industry allowance) from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026. This rate applies to ordinary hours and is set by the Fair Work Commission. For casual employees, a 25% loading is added, making the casual rate $38.84 per hour.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual pay from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, $31.07 × 38 × 52 = $61,394.32. This assumes the same rate every week with no overtime or allowances.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate?
faqs.a: No. Superannuation is paid on top of the hourly rate. Under the Waste Management Award, employers must contribute at least 12% of ordinary earnings to a super fund, up to the maximum contribution base ($270,830 for 2026–27). For a Level 3 driver earning $61,394, the super contribution would be about $7,367 per year.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Garbage Truck Driver Salary

If you're looking for a **garbage truck driver salary**, the starting point is the Waste Management Award 2020 (MA000043). This award covers employees in the waste management industry, including drivers who collect, transport, and dispose of waste. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides that summarise the minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates for each classification.

For a full-time adult employee at Level 3 (a common classification for experienced drivers), the ordinary hourly rate is **$31.07** as of 1 July 2026. This rate already includes the industry allowance of $3.24 per hour. The weekly pay for a 38-hour week is **$1,180.58**, and the fortnightly pay is **$2,361.16**.

## Award Rates vs. National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. The garbage truck driver award rate is higher because it reflects the skills and conditions of the job. Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission after annual wage reviews and are legally enforceable. Employers must pay at least the award rate for the classification, or a higher enterprise agreement rate if one applies.

## Hourly to Annual: The Calculation

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the formula:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time garbage truck driver working 38 ordinary hours per week:

$31.07 × 38 × 52 = **$61,394.32** per year

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. If you work overtime or on weekends, your actual pay will be higher due to penalty rates (150% for the first 2 hours, 200% after that for full-time employees).

For part-time employees, the same hourly rate applies but with fewer hours. Casual employees get a 25% loading on top of the ordinary rate, making the casual rate **$38.84** per hour. The annual equivalent for a casual working 38 hours would be about $76,743, but casuals don't receive paid leave.

## Casual Loading and Super

Casual employees under the Waste Management Award are entitled to a 25% loading on the ordinary hourly rate, as per clause 11.4. This loading compensates for the lack of annual leave, personal leave, and other entitlements. The casual loading is paid on top of the base rate, so you should never enter a rate that already includes casual loading when using a calculator.

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your gross pay. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a full-time Level 3 driver earning $61,394, the employer must contribute approximately **$7,367** per year to a super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional cost to the employer.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on your total taxable income and the tax rates for 2026–27. The Australian Taxation Office uses a progressive tax scale:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on the excess over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners).

For a garbage truck driver earning $61,394 per year, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be around **$11,750**, leaving a take-home pay of about **$49,644** per year, or **$4,137** per month. This is an estimate; your actual tax may vary based on deductions, HELP repayments, or the Medicare levy surcharge.

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then calculates annual gross pay, super, and estimated tax. Remember to enter the ordinary hourly rate (without casual loading) and check the casual box if applicable. For award-covered roles like garbage truck driving, always use the rate from the [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).

You can also explore [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) comparisons, [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimates, and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) information. For other occupations, see [average pay](/topics/average-pay) or [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion).

## Conclusion

The garbage truck driver salary under the Waste Management Award provides a clear minimum. For a Level 3 full-time employee, the hourly rate is $31.07, leading to an annual gross of about $61,394. Casual employees earn $38.84 per hour including loading. Super is paid on top, and tax reduces take-home pay. Always check the latest award rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman, as they change each July.
